name: feroxbuster
summary: A recursive content discovery tool that brute-forces web paths with a wordlist to find unlinked resources on web servers.
use_cases: enumerate hidden directories and files on a web application
scan URLs read from stdin and pipe results to another tool
features: append file extensions to each URL
route traffic through HTTP or SOCKS proxies
send custom headers and request bodies

steps.purpose: run install script into ~/.local/bin (downloads x86_64-linux release zip)
run install script into ~/.local/bin (downloads x86_64-linux release zip)

smoke_tests.command: feroxbuster -u http://127.0.0.1:8000 -w /tmp/ft/words.txt --no-state --no-recursion -x pdf -x js,html -x php txt json,docx

pitfalls.actually_needed: Script also tries fc-list/fc-cache to install an emoji font; they are absent here and print 'command not found', but the install still succeeds (font file is dropped in ~/.fonts)
Default wordlist is a SecLists path not present outside Kali; pass -w <wordlist> explicitly
The target directory must exist first (mkdir -p $HOME/.local/bin); the script unzips into it

judge.observed: All three checks exited 0 with their expected signals: the first scan found /admin/secret (200), the extension scan found /backup.php (200), and -V printed 'feroxbuster 2.14.0'.

what_it_does.quote: `feroxbuster` uses brute force combined with a wordlist to search for unlinked content in target directories.

who_it_is_for.quote: `feroxbuster` is a tool designed to perform [Forced Browsing](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Forced_browsing).

config_and_keys.quote: Installing from the repos adds a [**ferox-config.toml**](https://epi052.github.io/feroxbuster-docs/configuration/ferox-config-toml/) in `/etc/feroxbuster/`

evidence.quote: A simple, fast, recursive content discovery tool written in Rust
